Subject: HealthSync DPA signature path + conditional routing plan

Hi Peter / HealthSync legal team,

Thanks for the call this morning — good alignment on scope. To keep momentum, here are the concrete next steps we propose so the DPA (with SCCs / UK IDTA considerations) and any routing constraints are finalized before the POC starts: 

- Redwood sends a redline of the DPA reflecting the SCP/SCCs + UK addendum crossover language (attached).
- HealthSync reviews redline; confirm whether the primary requirement is: (A) SCCs with TIA supplements for EU residency, or (B) UK IDTA + UK addendum for UK-resident data.
- If HealthSync needs an elevated residency guarantee, we propose a conditional routing policy: onshore cache + EU region processing for EU/UK user data; default hosted routing otherwise.
- Sign-off cadence: legal review by 4/13, DocuSign by 4/15, go/no-go for POC by 4/19.

Questions for HealthSync: can you confirm the subset of personal data streams that must be routed to EU/UK? Also, please share any procurement-required evidence (SOC 2 report, subprocessor list acceptance form).

I’ve copied Laura and Kimberly from our legal/privacy teams to handle the DPA/transfer mechanics. Logan (cc’d) will prepare an ops note for conditional routing if you need it.

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: HealthSync DPA signature path + conditional routing plan

Ben, Laura — thanks for the summary. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- HealthSync needs UK addendum language for UK-resident profiles and SCCs for pan-EU processing. We expect both to be reflected; we call that a dual path.
- We will require a TIA/DTIA-style technical appendix showing that onshore cache + EU region processing is enforceable (routing controls, logging, and sampling). A high-level TIA is fine to start.
- Subprocessors: the attached procurement questionnaire wants a CSV and an attestation that none of the subprocessors will themselves export to third countries without notice. Can Redwood provide a short attestation and the CSV you referenced?

Also: our legal team flagged section 6.3 (data export safeguards) — they prefer specific fallback behavior if UK addendum cannot be applied for a subset of traffic (e.g., automatic escalation to an approved dedicated pool).

We can try to hit your 4/13 review timeline but may need until 4/14 depending on procurement. I’ll loop in Legal Contracts on any redline notes.

Best,
Peter Walsh
Head of Platform Integrations, HealthSync
peter.walsh@healthsync.com

Hi Peter / HealthSync legal,

Thanks — attached is our redline (HealthSync_DPA_v3_redline.pdf). A few notes to speed review: 

1) Dual-path transfer model: we built language so the contract can reference both SCCs (for EU processing) and the UK IDTA/UK addendum for UK-resident data. We added a short clause that requires HealthSync to mark which data subjects/events are in-scope for the UK addendum.

2) Technical Implementation Appendix (TIA): I’ve drafted a one-page TIA summary in the redline (page 4) outlining required controls — routing selectors, per-request region header, audit log sampling, and an ops escalation path to an approved dedicated pool if routing fails. This is intentionally operational and not a complete engineering spec.

3) Subprocessors: Redwood’s current roster is attached (Redwood_Subprocessor_List_Mar2027.csv). We will provide an attestation letter that subprocessors will not export HealthSync-marked EU/UK personal data outside permitted regions without prior notice/approval. That attestation is contingent on HealthSync confirming the data categories you must protect.

4) Fallback behavior: proposed contractual fallback is an automatic shift to a reserved-dedicated pool (subject to capacity & commercial agreement) — we noted that procurement may require a separate reserved capacity addendum.

If HealthSync accepts the redline in principle, we suggest executing via DocuSign (link below) and proceeding with a 2-week ops sprint to implement the routing selectors and sample logs. Please mark any redline points you want us to re-open — we can prioritize the TIA appendix and section 6.3 fallback language.

DocuSign envelope preview: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/ABCD1234

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection
